rounds.text: Vellora Impact Ltd trades at a microscopic market capitalization of just ₹ 8.20 Cr [E1], heavily compressed near its 52-week low [E3, E26], which creates an asymmetric deep-value entry point for a micro-cap operating in an exceptionally strong macro environment. The business benefits directly from a powerful sector tailwind in Chemicals with a tailwind score of +0.76 [E29, E30], backed by robust industry expansion where sector median sales growth sits at 15.3% and sector median profit growth surges at 41.7% [E31, E32]. Operational momentum is already showing tangible green shoots at the fundamental level, as demonstrated by sales increasing quarter-over-quarter [E25] within a non-cyclical earnings profile [E21]. Furthermore, long-term historical performance proves the underlying business model is capable of wealth creation, delivering a compounded share price growth of 21% over 10 years [E4]. Conceded: promoter holding has collapsed by 42.86 percentage points down to 3.12% [E9], the relative-strength rating languishes at 0 [E15], and the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E14].

Vellora Impact Ltd presents a severe investment risk characterized by catastrophic insider abandonment, with promoter holdings plunging from 45.98% in September 2023 down to a negligible 3.12% by June 2026 [E9]. This massive 42.86 percentage point reduction signals a profound lack of confidence from those closest to the business [E9, E23]. Compounding this alarming governance signal, the rules-based screen firmly rates the stock a SELL at 33 out of 100 with low confidence [E24]. Investors face brutal downward momentum accompanied by extreme annualised volatility of 81.8% and a devastating historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -91.3% [E17, E18]. Long-term wealth destruction is evident across multiple horizons, with compounded share price growth sitting at -2% over 5 years, -15% over 3 years, and -29% over 1 year, paired with a relative-strength rating of zero against the Nifty 500 and a complete absence of dividend payouts [E2, E5, E6, E7, E15]. Finally, the current pricing near the 52-week low provides a strategic entry point right as the non-cyclical earnings profile and sector tailwinds align to re-rate the micro-cap market capitalisation of ₹ 8.20 Cr [E1, E3, E21, E26, E30].

However, pointing to a 10-year compounded growth rate of 21% [E4] ignores the severe deterioration in recent periods, specifically 5-year, 3-year, and 1-year compounded share price growth of -2%, -15%, and -29% respectively [E5, E6, E7]. The bull's reliance on quarter-over-quarter sales gains [E25] is completely undermined by inconsistent quarterly operating margins over the last two quarters [E8], invalidating any thesis of sustainable operational momentum. Furthermore, dismissing extreme volatility [E18] and an all-time worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -91.3% [E17] is reckless when the stock is trapped below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E14] with an absolute relative-strength rating of zero [E15]. Finally, a micro-cap valuation of ₹ 8.20 Cr [E1] sitting near its 52-week low [E3, E12, E26] does not represent a strategic entry point given that promoters have aggressively dumped their stake from 45.98% to a negligible 3.12% [E9, E23], triggering a failing rules-based screen score of 33 out of 100 [E24].
